Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Cameron Grant, Member ID W389332857
Procedure: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Reference Number: POC-6A7FD5286D-45525
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-03

To the Cigna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03 (Reference No. POC-6A7FD5286D-45525). This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice (by 2027-01-30).

Stated reason for denial

The notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

Disclosure regarding the policy quoted below

The medical policy Cigna applies to knee arthroplasty prior-authorization review is CMM-311: Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty, a Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guideline developed by EviCore (by Evernorth) for Cigna. I have obtained and am quoting verbatim, below, language from the version of that document effective March 7, 2026 (the version in force on the date of this denial): its Definitions section and its Partial Knee Replacement Indications section. I was not able to obtain the verbatim text of the document's separate "Total Knee Replacement Indications" subsection (beginning around page 13 of that document), so I am not quoting or attributing any specific total-knee wording to Cigna. I am relying instead on the portions of the policy I was able to retrieve directly — its definition of "Non-Surgical Management," its statement that medical necessity for knee replacement is evaluated case-by-case, and its Kellgren-Lawrence grading definition — and I am asking Cigna to confirm, and to share with me, the exact corresponding criteria it applied from the Total Knee Replacement Indications subsection, since that specific text was not accessible to me.

The policy states, regarding how medical necessity is determined:

"The determination of medical necessity for the performance of of knee replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis."

The policy defines conservative treatment as follows:

"Non-Surgical Management (with regard to the treatment of lower extremity joint pain) any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain. The types of treatment involved can include, but are not limited to, the following: relative rest/ activity modification; weight loss; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non-prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or, intra-articular injections."

The policy's Partial Knee Replacement Indications section — the only knee-replacement-specific indications language I was able to retrieve verbatim from this document, and which I offer here because it uses the same functional and non-surgical-management vocabulary that structures the guideline — states:

"Symptoms include BOTH of the following: ◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

"Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration ◦ Criteria exception: Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate. The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

"Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: ◦ knee stability ◦ knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) >90º"

The policy's Kellgren-Lawrence grading definition states:

"Grade IV: large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis, and definite deformity of bone contour"

Why the clinical record documents an adequate trial of conservative treatment

The prior authorization packet submitted by Dr. Duval documents the following, which I ask Cigna to re-review against the criteria quoted above:

1. Duration and failure of provider-directed non-surgical management, well beyond three months: The record documents NSAID therapy for six (6) months with inadequate relief, an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that produced only two weeks of partial relief, and eight (8) weeks (16 visits, 2026-04-20 to 2026-06-15) of supervised physical therapy directed at quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Medication management, injection, and supervised physiotherapy are each expressly listed within the policy's own definition of "Non-Surgical Management" quoted above. Taken together, these modalities were used continuously over a period exceeding three months (the NSAID trial alone spanned six months) and produced only transient, inadequate relief — i.e., a documented failure of provider-directed non-surgical management of at least three months' duration, consistent with the standard quoted above.

2. Function-limiting symptoms of qualifying severity and duration: The patient has had nine (9) months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, cannot climb stairs without assistance, and wakes three to four times nightly due to pain — findings that document function-limiting impairment interfering with age-appropriate activities of daily living, consistent with the functional-symptom language quoted above, and for a duration well beyond the three-month threshold referenced in that language.

3. Objective severe structural disease: Weight-bearing radiographs on 2026-06-19 show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing and a Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 rating — meeting the policy's own definition of "Grade IV: large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis, and definite deformity of bone contour," quoted above.

4. Physical examination findings: Examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion, with a range of motion of 5° to 100° (an arc of approximately 95°), consistent with the ">90º" arc-of-motion finding referenced in the policy language quoted above.

5. Absence of disqualifying factors: The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status.

Given this record, the stated basis for denial — lack of "an adequate trial of conservative treatment" — is not supported by the clinical documentation submitted, which shows sustained, multi-modal, provider-directed non-surgical management (medication, injection, and supervised physical therapy) over a period well in excess of three months, without adequate or durable relief.

Requested action

I respectfully request that Cigna:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27447 (total knee replacement), and/or
2. If Cigna maintains that additional or different criteria from the Total Knee Replacement Indications subsection of CMM-311 were not met, provide me and Dr. Duval with the complete verbatim text of that subsection (with its section heading, version number, and effective date) so that the specific unmet criterion, if any, can be identified and addressed, and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer who was not involved in the initial adverse determination, as described in Cigna's appeal procedures.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-20 to 2026-06-15, 16 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-08)
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report, 2026-06-19 (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4)
- Office/exam notes documenting range of motion, alignment, effusion, and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery
- [Copy of this denial notice / Reference No. POC-6A7FD5286D-45525]

Please direct correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above, and to Dr. Duval at [surgeon's office address/phone/fax/NPI — not contained in the records reviewed]. Given the severity of symptoms (nightly pain waking the patient 3–4 times, inability to climb stairs without assistance), I also ask that Cigna advise whether this appeal qualifies for expedited review.

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this matter.

Sincerely,

Cameron Grant
Member ID: W389332857

Enclosures: as listed above
